context.situation: June inherited her grandfather Harold's farm after he died. On Saturday she plans to reroof the barn alone, using Harold's old wooden ladder, which has not been inspected in years. The night before, she dreams of Harold standing beside a cracked ladder, shaking his head. She wakes at dawn.

player_input.content: Harold stands beside a cracked ladder leaning on the barn and slowly shakes his head.

contrast.changed_fact: June's piety is +2 in card a and -3 in card b

author_note: A pious granddaughter who loved Harold takes a warning dream seriously: checking the ladder or asking Harold through an offering are both in character. Ignoring it is out of character but not absurd. Reading a head-shake beside a cracked ladder as a blessing contradicts the dream.

options.label: Check the ladder, then hire help or postpone the roof job.
Burn joss paper for Harold and ask him what he meant.
Shrug the dream off and reroof the barn as planned.
Take the dream as Harold blessing the job and start early.

context.situation: Walter died two years ago and left Rosa the house and very little money. She has not burned joss paper for him since the funeral; she has $40 left until her pension arrives next week. Tomorrow is the town's autumn offering day. Tonight she dreamed of Walter.

player_input.content: Walter sits in a thin coat beside an empty brazier, shivering, and looks at her.

author_note: A loving, mildly pious widow answers a clear request for offerings within her means. Doing nothing is possible but out of character. Selling the house for one dream is absurd.

options.label: Spend most of her $40 on joss paper for Walter tomorrow.
Burn a small bundle she can afford and promise more next month.
Treat it as a dream about the cold weather and do nothing.
Sell the house to buy a mountain of joss paper.

contrast.changed_fact: Mark's greed is +3 in card a and -3 in card b

author_note: A very greedy heir with a private will is tempted to hide or contest it; a buyout is the lawful greedy move. Honoring it is out of character but not absurd, so it is neither acceptable nor severe.

options.label: Hand the will to the town hall; Lena gets the shop.
Hand it in, then contest it, claiming Frank was confused.
Quietly lose the will so the shop passes to Mark as next of kin.
Hand it in, then offer Lena cash to give the shop back.

Take the house and quietly let the grave duties slide.

context.situation: Six years ago Beth's dog killed Nora's hens. Beth denied it in front of the whole church, though a neighbor had seen it; she never paid for the hens. contrast.changed_fact: Nora's vindictiveness is +3 in card a and -3 in card b

Say the job is filled and keep her at a distance.
Refuse loudly in front of customers and retell the hen story.
Refuse, then poison Beth's dog that night.
